biod: fix closed fake biometric pipe from live locking the message loop The named pipe used by FakeBiometric for input is added to the message loop in order for it to get signaled when there is input. Due to the way pipes work, a poll on their FD will always trigger a POLLHUP after the pipe is opened writable and closed, which fake_biometric_tool does. Because this constantly happens, no other events could make it through the message loop. The workaround is to open the pipe read/write in FakeBiometric to ensure a writable end is always open, which prevents POLLHUP. biod: add GetId() to biometric interface Due to some fun with race conditions and removing arbitrary Enrollments at any time, a stable ID is required to reference Enrollment objects on DBus. More specifically, the sequence below led to an issue 1) a client gets a list of enrollments, which originally were just named in order of the returned vector from GetEnrollments 2) removed enrollment N in the middle of the vector 3) removed enrollment N+1 Enrollment that was originally N+1 would actually be enrollment N after the removal, leading to unwanted results for the client. The usage of a stable ID supplied by the Biometric upon enrollment nicely sidesteps this problem. BUG=None TEST=Enrollment IDs don't change after removing an enrollment from a Biometric Change-Id: Iee65ef81d810e6a8159268f18659aa302d313a78 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/384640 Commit-Ready: Zach Reizner <zachr@chromium.org> Tested-by: Zach Reizner <zachr@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Chirantan Ekbote <chirantan@chromium.org>

glibc: add clang-style FORTIFY. This patch adds support for a clang-style FORTIFY to ChromeOS's glibc. Without this, when we swap to clang as the default compiler for ChromeOS, our FORTIFY story will get *way* worse. When given a gcc-style FORTIFY, clang is unable to emit just about any compile-time diagnostics, and the dynamic checks that clang emits is a (small) subset of gcc's. This patch makes clang's diagnostic story nearly on-par with gcc's, and should allow clang to dynamically catch just about any bug that gcc can (either statically or dynamically). Due to differences in how the compilers work (e.g. how they optimize code, etc.), there may be cases where clang detects errors at run-time where gcc can't and vice-versa. CHROMIUM: usb: dwc3: support host mode for rockchip platform Add a rockchip specific glue layer to support usb3 HOST only mode for rk3399 gru board. This patch depends on DWC3 core runtime PM. With this patch, we can support for XHCI integrated in DWC3 IP on rockchip platforms. It depends on extcon notifier to do runtime suspend and runtime resume. Since the DWC3 rockchip device is the parent of DWC3 core device, so we need to allow runtime PM for DWC3 rockchip device and DWC3 core device. And if we do runtime suspend/resume for DWC3 core device, the PM core will also do its parents runtime suspend/resume. The runtime PM is useful for rockchip XHCI, because we need to assert a specific controller reset before PHY init, and after PHY init successfully, we can deassert controller reset, and reinit XHCI and DWC3 core controller via runtime PM callbacks. We can also manage DWC3 IP power domain and clocks in runtime PM. It's helpful for power saving. Note, because runtime PM is not perfect and stable in xhci-plat, so we use add/remove hcd instead of runtime PM for XHCI reinit. groeck: - Use local functions for chip access to enable build as module without having to export various functions from the core. - Do not power off/on usb2 phy as (currently) not needed. - Check dr_mode once prior to installing extcon notifier, and don't keep checking it (it is not expected to change). - No error message when exiting with -EPROBE_DEFER. - Cancel worker on exit. - Disable clock on exit if not suspended. - Remove and re-insert hcd in extcon worker function to avoid crash on module unload. - Get devicetree properties early in probe function to simplify error handling. - Don't call pm_runtime_set_suspended() on removal. It causes warning tracebacks from the clock subsystem. Call pm_runtime_forbid() instead to ensure no runtime activity occurs while removing clocks. - Don't abort on errors in the extcon worker. It is important to reinstall the HCDs to avoid a crash when unloading the driver. - Add a slight delay after deasserting reset and before adding HCDs. This was seen to improve device discovery.
